clauses.reason: The final paragraph approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Feed Manufacturing Industry, with a proviso on the Association's participation in selecting the Code Authority: "do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Feed Manufacturing Industry, provided that the continued participation of the American Feed Manufacturers' Association, Inc. in the selection of the Code Authority, after June 1, 1934 shall be contingent upon its amendment of its by-laws to the satisfaction of the Secretary of Agriculture and the Administrator for Industrial Recovery". The clause depends on the approved code for its effect: under section 3(b) of Title I "provisions of such code shall be the standards of fair competition" for the trade or industry. S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides in section 2 that "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed", so this command had no operative effect after June 14, 1935. The resolution states no deferred effective date (it ends "Approved, June 14, 1935."), and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 replaced the two-year expiry with "April 1, 1936". Schechter (decided May 27, 1935) held the section 3 code-making authority an unconstitutional delegation; that is recorded as a validity characterization and not as an end date.

inventory_overrides.reason: Items 1 through 5 of the numbered list are findings that recite the basis for approval and command nothing; the operative command is the final Now, Therefore paragraph approving the code, which is the only clause.

research_rationale:
This order is a presidential approval, under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, of the Code of Fair Competition for the Feed Manufacturing Industry: "do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Feed Manufacturing Industry, provided that the continued participation of the American Feed Manufacturers' Association, Inc. in the selection of the Code Authority, after June 1, 1934 shall be contingent upon its amendment of its by-laws to the satisfaction of the Secretary of Agriculture and the Administrator for Industrial Recovery". Its only legal effect depended on that code (NIRA section 3(b) made the code's provisions the standards of fair competition). Congress approved S.J. Res. 113 on June 14, 1935, and section 2 repealed the provisions of Title I that delegated power to approve or prescribe codes and provided for their enforcement, so the approval had no operative effect after that date. Schechter's May 27, 1935 holding that the section 3 delegation was unconstitutional is recorded as a validity characterization and not as an end date, following the reviewed shared analysis. The text relied on is the American Presidency Project transcription, so the original is not yet held and the quotation must be re-checked when an official copy is retrieved.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code before June 14, 1935 are accrued effects of the approval. Section 5 of Title I exempted a code approved and in effect under the title, and complying action, from the antitrust laws while the title was in effect "and for sixty days thereafter"; whatever exemption survives for past action is an accrued effect. The proviso to section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 names agreements and action thereunder, not codes, and states no time limit, so the held text does not settle its reach. No held source continues the approval itself after June 14, 1935.
